newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND IN CONTROL AT TEA BUT NZ FIGHTING.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND IN CONTROL AT TEA BUT NZ FIGHTING.

text.p: England were in firm control at tea on the third day of the second cricket test against New Zealand on Saturday although they suffered a minor batting collapse just before the interval.
The tourists were 350 for the loss of seven wickets at tea, a 226-run lead after the home side scored just 124 in their first innings. Darren Gough was unbeaten on 14 and Dominic Cork on four.

England resumed after the lunch break at 282 for four and looked ominous as left-hander Graham Thorpe raced to his second consecutive test hundred of the series and John Crawley passed his half-century.
But three wickets fell in the space of 20 balls shortly before the break.

Thorpe fell to a sharp stumping while facing off-spinner Dipak Patel on 108. He left his crease momentarily for a drive only to be beaten by Patel's turn and keeper Lee Germon quickly had the bails off.
Thorpe batted for 329 minutes, faced 249 balls and hit 12 boundaries for his fourth test hundred, and together with Crawley added 118 in 180 minutes for the fifth wicket.
In the next over, Crawley edged fast-medium bowler Simon Doull to Germon after making 56, then Robert Croft was caught off Doull at first slip without scoring.
Doull had taken four for 59 with one wicket apiece to Geoff Allott, Patel and Daniel Vettori.
